links.targetTitle: Aligned Delegates are forbidden from voting for an emergency

title: The decision to fire an emergency power and the attestation that it is authentic are held by different parties
content:
A.1.10.5.2.3.1 reserves the initiation decision narrowly: "The decision to initiate the process to use a Standby Spell is reserved for the Core Facilitator," who is also responsible for validating and categorizing the emergency scenario in the first place, and who then actions the spell and liaises with Ranked Delegates to gather support.

A.1.10.5.2.3.2.1 places a separate gate on the same action: "Two Authorized Representatives... from Core GovOps must validate the authenticity of the Standby Spell," in written form in the secure Emergency Response channel, and only named representatives may supply that validation.

The split matters because the two questions are genuinely different. *Should we act?* is a judgment call about the incident, which needs a single accountable decision-maker so it can be made in minutes. *Is this the spell it claims to be?* is a verification question, which must not be answered by whoever is under pressure to act.

The consequence is that no single role can both declare an emergency and certify the artifact used to respond to it. Under time pressure the natural failure is for the decision-maker's urgency to substitute for verification — and the Atlas structurally forbids that substitution by putting the attestation in another team's hands and requiring it in writing, on the record.
description: Only the Core Facilitator may initiate a Standby Spell, but two Authorized Representatives of Core GovOps must independently validate its authenticity in writing before delegates may vote.
